title: Key-value pair
description: One entry in the platform's datastore. Stored in the document store, served over the REST API, and substituted into action parameters and rule criteria by name.

uid.description: The platform-wide uid of the record, which encodes its resource type and name.

name.description: The key an automation refers to. Together with the scope it is the identity of the entry.

description.description: Free text for whoever finds the key later.

value.description: Always characters. A stored secret is ciphertext here; a masked read answers with a placeholder instead.

secret.description: On write, a request to store the value encrypted; an installation with no key file refuses the write.

encrypted.description: On write, an assertion that the supplied value is already ciphertext — it forces secret on. On read, a computed fact: the value in this response was not decrypted for the caller.

scope.description: Which namespace the entry lives in. The default is the system-wide scope; the per-user scope is how one key name means different things to different operators.

expire-timestamp.description: When the entry stops being readable, derived from the time-to-live given at write time. Wire key: expire_timestamp.

ttl.description: Seconds to live. Input only — the source says so in a note beside the field; a stored entry reports the timestamp instead.
